title: What Is Prana? Meaning in Yoga and Ayurveda
h1: What Is Prana? Meaning in Yoga and Ayurveda
excerpt: Prana is a Sanskrit term for breath or vitality in yoga and Ayurveda. It is a traditional concept, not a measured gas or a product.

quick_answer.question: What is prana?
quick_answer.answer: Prana is a Sanskrit word for breath and for a vitality that yoga and Ayurveda treat as more than air. Traditions map it through the body. Physiology has not established that map as a force.

intro: Prana is the word English speakers meet when a yoga class talks about energy in the breath. The word is older and broader than that class. It is not a brand of oxygen.

sections.heading: What does prana mean?
sections.content:
In Sanskrit usage, prana can mean breath, life, and a vitality said to move through channels. Ayurveda and yoga share the vocabulary and do not always draw the same diagrams. Britannica's short article is a public orientation. The glossary entry is the compact version.

The neighboring page is [the prana glossary](/glossary/prana/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: How do practices use the idea?
sections.content:
Classical yoga lists pranayama, regulation of breath, as a limb of practice. Hatha texts add techniques and cautions. Those texts assume a teacher and a cosmology. An app timer is not that setting, even when it uses the word.

A wider map lives at the [breathwork topic](/topics/breathwork/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: What should it not be confused with?
sections.content:
Quietly noticing the breath does not require you to believe in a life-force substance. Forceful breathing and long holds are a different risk and still do not prove the substance. If you have a heart or lung condition, ask a clinician before you alter breathing on purpose.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [how traditions describe prana](/questions/how-do-traditions-describe-prana/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not buy a product because it claims to increase prana. Do not treat tingling from fast breathing as a spiritual credential. Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and attention explain a great deal without a second anatomy.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: It is not identical to oxygen.
Breath exercises do not prove the cosmology.

faq.answer: No. It is an educational explanation. Health decisions belong with a qualified professional.
